title: AWS Free Tier: What Actually Costs Money

cover.alt: Conceptual still life of a powered-down server, a connected storage cartridge, and a cost alert bell.

figures.title: The resource layers worth checking
figures.summary: An application can stop running while related storage or transfer activity still deserves attention.

items.label: Compute
items.detail: Inspect instances and the resources associated with them.

items.label: Databases
items.detail: Check database instances and retained storage.

items.label: Object storage
items.detail: Review accumulated uploads and old build artifacts.

items.label: Functions
items.detail: Inspect invocation patterns, duration, and configuration.

items.label: Transfer
items.detail: Look for downloads and activity between regions.

figures.caption: Resource categories from this article. Current allowances and prices are intentionally not reproduced.

figures.title: Three checks before walking away
figures.summary: Cost visibility requires both an inventory of resources and a way to notice unexpected usage.

items.label: Know what exists
items.detail: Review running instances, databases, storage, and any resources in other regions.

items.label: Confirm the alert
items.detail: Check that the budget and email notification are configured.

items.label: Review the cost view
items.detail: Group recent costs by service and investigate unfamiliar entries.

figures.caption: Budget alerts notify; they do not stop charges or guarantee that usage remains free.
